questions.q: When is a design solution considered to be most appropriate?
options: When it satisfies the aesthetic requirements
When it meets the needs of the target market
When it provides strength, durability and safety
When it fulfils its intended end-use requirements
questions.explanation: A design solution is judged most appropriate when it successfully fulfils its intended end-use or functional requirements. Aesthetics, durability and meeting the target market are individual design factors, but appropriateness is measured against the intended purpose.

questions.q: Designers obtain patents to protect their designs to ensure
options: effective marketing controls.
the safe production of their designs.
the effective international marketing of their designs.
exclusive rights to license, promote and sell their designs.
questions.explanation: A patent is a form of intellectual property protection that grants the owner exclusive rights to make, use, license and sell an invention. It protects ownership of the design rather than guaranteeing marketing or safe production.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important factor when considering the sustainability of a material for the manufacture of a product?
options: The durability of the selected material
The cost of manufacturing the product
The ability of the material to be renewed
The effect of a carbon tax on manufacturing the product
questions.explanation: Sustainability of a material depends most on whether it can be renewed, ensuring long-term resource availability and reduced environmental impact. Durability and cost are relevant design factors but do not directly address sustainability.

questions.q: Emerging technologies provide designers with unique opportunities to
options: develop products that are innovative.
develop products that guarantee increased sales.
design products that have a limited range of inbuilt applications.
design products using existing technologies that have proved to be successful.
questions.explanation: Emerging technologies open up new possibilities that allow designers to create genuinely innovative products. They cannot guarantee sales, and relying on existing or limited applications is the opposite of using emerging technology.

questions.q: Effective product development relies mainly upon
options: selecting a suitable manufacturing process.
the ability of designers to sketch original ideas.
the ability of designers to manage financial issues.
gathering ongoing evaluation and responding to feedback.
questions.explanation: Effective product development depends on continuous evaluation and responding to feedback throughout the design process, allowing the product to be refined to meet user needs. The other options are individual skills or stages within development.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of conducting market research prior to product development?
options: To formulate finance and action plans
To determine suitable advertising methods
To identify the needs and wants of the target audience
To determine the values and beliefs of various cultural groups
questions.explanation: Market research carried out before development is a needs analysis that identifies the needs and wants of the target audience so the product is appropriate for them. Finance plans and advertising decisions come later in the process.

questions.q: Which combination of factors most influences the success of an innovation?
options: Social demand and cultural values
Product demand and social implications
Timing and appropriate marketing strategies
Ease of use and economical manufacturing processes
questions.explanation: The success of an innovation depends largely on timing — releasing the product when the market is ready — combined with appropriate marketing strategies to reach consumers. Even a strong product can fail if it is mistimed or poorly marketed.

questions.q: Which of the following best indicates that a product is becoming obsolete?
options: When innovative design features are incorporated
When the product has been superseded by a newer design
When there is a decrease in the product’s sales and turnover
When the product has undergone modifications to improve its function
questions.explanation: Obsolescence occurs when a product is superseded by a newer or improved design and is no longer wanted. Falling sales can be a symptom of many things, but supersession is the clearest indicator of obsolescence.

questions.q:
The graph shows information relating to four different production processes (A, B, C and D) being considered for use by a designer for mass production of a product. The graph compares, for each process, the number of tools/equipment, speed of operations, number of operations and accuracy of output.

From a designer’s perspective, which production process is most likely to efficiently manufacture a quality product?
options: A
B
C
D
questions.explanation: Reading the graph, the most efficient quality process combines high speed and accuracy of output while requiring the fewest tools/equipment and operations, which is shown by process A. Interpreting such comparative data is a key part of communication and decision-making in design.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most ethically sound consideration for a designer to take into account when developing a new product?
options: Embracing the cultural aspects of the community
Improving the lives and workplace practices for a majority of the stakeholders
Increasing the overall economic benefits for the manufacturer by increasing sales
Reducing the environmental issues and increasing the sustainability issues for the manufacturer
questions.explanation: The most ethically sound consideration is improving the lives and workplace practices for the majority of stakeholders, prioritising people and social responsibility. Purely economic gain for the manufacturer is not primarily an ethical consideration.

questions.q: Why is it important to consider a product’s function during its development?

criteria.descriptor: Sketches in general terms why consideration of function is important during the development of a product
Identifies a functional factor

questions.modelAnswer: In designing a new product the designer must ensure it meets its intended purpose. For example, a sports water bottle must be light, easy to carry and not leak. Functional factors such as these are important considerations for the designer throughout the development of the product.

questions.q: Why do many designers still use hand-sketching despite the availability of computer-based graphics programs?

criteria.descriptor: Explains the importance of the use of hand-sketching to the design process in preference to computer-based graphics programs with reference to the characteristics and features of hand-sketching processes
Sketches in general terms how hand-sketching processes are important in the design process
Identifies a feature of hand-sketching

questions.modelAnswer: Hand sketches allow the designer to externalise visual thoughts and ideas that cannot be expressed accurately in words. These quick sketches let the designer evolve their ideas and their understanding of the problem in almost real time, which in turn sparks further new ideas and lets others visualise the designer's non-verbal concepts. Computer-based graphics programs may not allow the same immediate, real-time feedback that hand-sketching gives the design and communication situation.

questions.q: Describe how action plans and ongoing evaluation processes work together to contribute to the development of a successful design.

criteria.descriptor: Provides characteristics and features of how action plans AND ongoing evaluation processes work together to contribute to a successful design
Provides characteristics and features of how action plans AND/OR evaluation processes contribute to a successful design
Sketches in general terms how action plans AND/OR evaluation processes contribute to a successful design, OR identifies a feature of action plans AND a feature of evaluation processes
Identifies a feature of action plans OR evaluation processes

questions.modelAnswer: As part of the design process the designer develops an action plan to organise an appropriate and efficient operation, sequencing tasks correctly so the project runs efficiently. Combined with an ongoing evaluation structure, this helps ensure a successful design: if ongoing evaluation is not carried out, development may fail to address concerns about important design factors such as function, cost or safety. Together, action plans and ongoing evaluation ensure the end product best meets the needs of the client and the consumer.

questions.q: Discuss how the use of technology has changed designers’ work practices.

criteria.descriptor: Identifies issues and provides points for and/or against how the use of technology has changed designers’ work practices
Shows sound understanding of how the use of technology has changed the designers’ work practices positively and/or negatively
Shows some understanding of how the use of technology has changed designers’ work practices
Shows a basic understanding of the use of technology in designers’ work practices

questions.modelAnswer: Designers now have access to a range of technologies that affect their work practices both positively and negatively. A positive example is computer modelling, which lets a designer electronically send design ideas almost anywhere in the world, enabling other stakeholders to collaborate in the development process. Because collaborators may be in different parts of the world, the design can receive continuous, 24-hour input. A negative aspect, however, is the high initial cost of establishing the technology and the ongoing costs of upgrading and training needed to maintain access to current technology.

questions.q: Explain how new technologies are affecting Australian lifestyles.

criteria.descriptor: Makes clear the relationship between Australian lifestyles and new technologies; shows thorough understanding of how new technologies are affecting Australian lifestyles
Provides advantages AND/OR disadvantages of new technologies with direct reference to the impact on Australian lifestyles
Shows some understanding of new technologies AND/OR how they are affecting Australian lifestyles
Identifies a feature of new technologies OR one of the effects of new technologies on Australian lifestyles

questions.modelAnswer: Advanced technologies have changed Australian lifestyles in both positive and negative ways. For example, tablet computers, smartphones and MP3 players allow people travelling on public transport to listen to music, watch programs, catch up on news, check social media or video chat, helping them relax on their journey. However, the same technology lets them check work emails, video conference with colleagues and review spreadsheets and forecasts, intruding on leisure time and preventing the relaxation normally expected during that time.

questions.topic: Social impact of technologies and design development
questions.q: Analyse the relationship between emerging technologies, society and a designer’s vision in regard to the development of a new product, system or environment.

criteria.descriptor: Draws out and relates implications of the relationship between a designer’s vision, emerging technologies and society with a direct link to the development of a new product, system or environment
Provides reasons why and/or how a designer’s vision, emerging technologies and society affect the development of a new product, system or environment
Identifies issues and provides evidence of how a designer’s vision, emerging technologies and society affect the development of a new product, system or environment
Provides characteristics and features of how TWO or more of emerging technologies, designer’s vision or society affect the development of a new product, system or environment
Sketches in general terms how a designer’s vision AND/OR emerging technologies AND/OR society affect the development of a new product, system or environment
Identifies a feature of a designer’s vision, emerging technology or societal impact

questions.modelAnswer: A unique and dependent relationship exists between a designer’s vision, emerging technologies and society, as each is reliant on the others to achieve a successful new product, system or environment. A designer’s vision to create a product that saves time in food preparation is inspired by feedback from working parents who lack time to cook — a societal change driven by the economic need for both parents to work. This time-poor society gives the designer the stimulus to develop ideas such as digital slow-cookers and food processors that wash, peel, prepare and cook within one device, with built-in timers so meals can be pre-set. However, these features are only made possible by emerging technologies: miniaturised computerised microchips enable pre-set, time-controlled cooking, while mechanical blades, mixers and heating elements enable the device to peel, chop and cook. Designers may release one version, gather consumer feedback, then refine it with improved features that better suit society's needs. The designer’s vision is therefore inspired by the needs of society and made possible by the availability of emerging technologies, showing the three elements are mutually dependent in developing a successful product.
